title: Pregnancy Recipes: Iron-and-Folate Bowls You Can Cook in 30 Minutes
excerpt: Three tasty recipes pairing heme/non-heme iron with vitamin C — Vietnamese-inspired bowls with clear amounts and food-safety notes.
content:
## Introduction
During pregnancy, it's essential to provide adequate iron and folate to ensure the health of both mother and baby. Iron helps create red blood cells, while folate supports fetal development. However, choosing iron- and folate-rich foods can be challenging. Here are three simple and delicious recipes that combine iron with vitamin C, which can be cooked in under 30 minutes.

## Recipe 1: Grilled Chicken and Vegetable Bowl with Lemon
* 100g grilled chicken (contains 1.5mg iron)
* 1 cup steamed broccoli (contains 2.5mg iron)
* 1 lemon (contains 53mg vitamin C)
* 1 cup cooked white rice
* 1 tablespoon olive oil
* Salt and pepper

Grill the chicken in the oven at 200°C for 20 minutes. Steam the broccoli in boiling water for 5 minutes. Mix all the ingredients together and squeeze the lemon on top.

## Recipe 2: Beef and Vegetable Stir-Fry Bowl with Bell Pepper
* 100g beef stir-fry (contains 2.5mg iron)
* 1 cup stir-fried bell pepper (contains 1.5mg iron)
* 1 cup cooked white rice
* 1 tablespoon olive oil
* Salt and pepper

Stir-fry the beef in a pan with olive oil for 5 minutes. Add the bell pepper and stir-fry for another 2 minutes. Mix all the ingredients together.

## Recipe 3: Baked Salmon and Vegetable Bowl with Orange
* 100g baked salmon (contains 1.5mg iron)
* 1 cup steamed spinach (contains 1.5mg iron)
* 1 orange (contains 70mg vitamin C)
* 1 cup cooked white rice
* 1 tablespoon olive oil
* Salt and pepper

Bake the salmon in the oven at 200°C for 15 minutes. Steam the spinach in boiling water for 3 minutes. Mix all the ingredients together and squeeze the orange on top.

## Food Safety Notes
During pregnancy, it's crucial to prioritize food safety to avoid the risk of food poisoning. Ensure that all ingredients are cooked thoroughly and hot before consumption. Avoid eating raw or undercooked foods, especially meat, eggs, and seafood.

## Conclusion
These three recipes are delicious and rich in iron and folate, making them perfect for pregnant women. Remember to always check the temperature and cooking time to ensure food safety. Additionally, pregnant women can explore our [meal planner](/planner) for more healthy and safe meal ideas throughout their pregnancy.
